## 2026-11-17 02:16 · The reviewer to the lead (SR Leagues review 2.185 (code): a removed game stays in the draft)

REVIEW of step 2.185 (lane/2.185-draft-put-back @ 6bf1a86 vs 7443bb1). I changed nothing in the repository; probes lived in .local/review and a temporary test file I deleted afterwards; `git status` is clean.

FINDINGS

1. Low, but it breaks the step's own claim. A crafted post makes the count say one thing and publishing do another. `rules/summarize-publish.ts:51` counts a recording going to null; `publish-schedule.ts:~113` skips it (`game.recording !== null`). Neither one compares teams. Proof (probe in my working copy, stand-in world): remove a published game, then post add-game with the SAME gameId, other teams and no recording. Result: toPublish=1 ("change how 1 game is recorded") and the grid shows the new teams. Publish answers `published` and writes a revision, but the public game is unchanged (old teams, recording final-score). The screen cannot do this today: the add form makes a fresh id, and Put it back re-adds the stored teams. Smallest fix: summarizePublish counts a recording change only when the draft's value is not null, as publish does. And add-game refuses an id the published schedule holds unless it is Put it back (same teams); or planPublication blocks a same-id game whose teams differ.
2. Low. Put it back after someone else discarded the draft is not refused. `run-schedule-action.ts:281` checks "already back" before checking for a draft. Proof (probe): remove a game, discard, then put-back answers {saved, game-already-back} with draft=null. The page then says "X is already back in the draft" under "There is no draft yet". Nothing is written. Fix: `if (view.draft === null) return {refused,'nothing-to-put-back'}` before that check. After a publish by someone else it is already refused plainly; I checked.
3. Low (comment and test cover). `stand-in-world-scheduling.ts:130` says "As the database", but `s` is one league's world, so the stand-in never sees another league's id. The other-league case is proven only by the memory helper and the database test (both good). Either reword the comment or leave it.

LANES THAT LAND FIRST (meaning, not only text)

- 2.180 team-bin: its `pageGrid(view: Pick<'result'|'clashes'> & Partial<Pick<'undated'>>)` wraps buildGrid. Merged as is, `removed` and `published` never reach it, so every struck game silently disappears. It is Partial, so the type check does not catch it; the merge must widen the Pick.
